column1: # versions.tsv (harbor#1426) — the one register of the runtimes, tools, libraries and GitHub Actions every governed repo pins.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Fourteen repos pinned the same things at different values: requires-python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, a
# .python-version of 3.14 in a repo that requires 3.11, ruff `>=0.4` beside `>=0.14`, three SHAs of actions/checkout and a mutable
# `@v5` tag in eight places on the path of the one required gate. yard's tools/pinned-third-party.toml already had the right
# semantics (a vetted pin, hold_at with a reason, upgrade-as-PR, never auto-merged) for one tool in one repo; this is that model
# for the box. The drift check (fleet's projects_orchestrator.versions) prints each repo's difference from this file, and a
# difference is either fixed or a row in the repo's exception file with its reason. A pin found in a repo that this file does not
# name is red (standard.version-registered, in the drift check), so a new tool cannot be pinned in only one place.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> axis <TAB> name <TAB> value <TAB> sha <TAB> hold_at <TAB> hold_reason <TAB> upgrade <TAB> note
#   name        what is pinned: python-floor and python-version-file for the interpreter, the package name for a tool or library,
#   value       the registered version. A runtime floor is the lowest version a repo may require (requires-python >=value); a
#               python-version-file is the exact version; a tool or library is the lowest specifier a repo may declare (>=value,
#               or ^value for an npm major); an action is the release tag its sha is
#   sha         the full 40-hex commit the action's tag points at, verified against the action's release; - for every other axis
#   hold_at     a release at or above which the update bot never proposes and a pin is refused; - when there is none
#   hold_reason why it is held (required when hold_at is set); - otherwise
#   upgrade     pr (the bot opens a PR, never auto-merged) | manual (a person bumps it; the bot ignores it)
#   note        the evidence or the decision behind the value
